Reviewer’s comments.
1. Based on the calculations from the review team, the multiples of
exposure obtained from the in-vitro phototoxicity range from 7-fold
(using the NOEC from the in-vitro study and the potential eye exposure
based on study KINE 220019-EXT) to as much as 198-fold (using the IC50
from the in-vitro study and the plasma exposure).
Using the tissue exposures measured in WD2008-00842-00, the
Applicant calculates slightly different multiples of exposure. Based on
IC50, the Applicant notes potential for phototoxicity at about 234-fold the
maximum clinical plasma concentration of elinzanetant. Based on
NOEC, the Applicant notes potential for phototoxicity at about 73-fold
the maximum clinical concentration. They also note, that based on the
distribution data in the quantitative whole-body autoradiography
(QWBA) study (melanin binding), the expected maximum clinical
concentration in the eye as well as in pigmented skin is still 37- or 15161

Reference ID: 5623053

NDA #219469

Edna Albuquerque, Ph.D.
Pratistha Tamrakar, Ph.D.
Sarah Lee, Ph.D.

times below the NOEC of the phototoxicity assay. The Applicant
concludes that no clinically relevant phototoxicity is to be expected in
these tissues.
2. Although the MOEs calculated by the Applicant and by the review team
appear to be high, they should be interpreted with caution because
elinzanetant concentrations in human pigmented tissues are derived
based on the distribution of elinzanetant to pigmented tissues (eyes and
skin) in rats treated with a single dose of elinzanetant. There is no data
to inform the extent of melanin-containing tissue accumulation after
repeated dosing with elinzanetant.
3. Elinzanetant has several characteristics that, per the Guidance for
Industry: S10 Photosafety Evaluation of Pharmaceuticals (January
2015), available at https://www.fda.gov/media/85076/download, make it a
potential phototoxicant:
a. It absorbs photons in the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum (290-700 nm).
i. One peak was detected at 321.4 nm with a calculated molar
extinction coefficient (MEC) of 3762.3 L•mol-1, which exceeds
the threshold of 1000 L•mol-1 for phototoxicity (Study Report R13578).
b. It distributes to and accumulates in melanin-rich tissues (see below;
Study Report R-13624; Study Report R-14368).
c. It is cytotoxic in the in-vitro Balb/c 3T3 neutral red uptake
phototoxicity assay, with an IC50 of 0.845 µg/mL and an NOEC of
0.316 µg/mL in presence of UV-A (Study Report R-13578).
4. Considering its light absorption characteristics, its ability to induce
cytotoxicity in the in-vitro Balb/c 3T3 neutral red uptake phototoxicity
assay, and its ability to distribute to and accumulate in melanin-rich
tissues, elinzanetant should be considered a potential phototoxicant.
5. In the pooled safety analysis of the 4 studies (SWITCH-1, and OASIS 1, 2
and 3), 5 women under elinzanetant 120 mg and 1 woman under placebo
treatment reported photosensitivity reaction (PTs). Of the 5, one had to
withdraw because of photosensitivity reaction (onset day 290). The
other 4 cases resolved despite continued treatment with elinzanetant
120 mg, and no actions were taken for these events.

NDA 219469 - Hepatobiliary toxicity (Q)SAR analysis for Elinzanetant
December 19, 2024

Elinzanetant, the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) from NDA 219469 and fezolinetant
(NDA 216578), another API in the same drug class, were evaluated by the
CDER/OTS/OCP/DARS Computational Toxicology Consultation Service (CTCS) for hepatobiliary
toxicity using (Q)SAR models. Three software programs were used to generate (Q)SAR
predictions for five hepatobiliary endpoints: Derek Nexus 6.4.1 (DX), Leadscope Model Applier
2023.0.3-3 (LMA), and CASE Ultra 1.9.2.1 (CU).
These are the most recent versions of the software. All (Q)SAR model outputs were reviewed
with the use of expert knowledge in order to provide additional supportive evidence on the
relevance of any positive, negative, conflicting or inconclusive prediction and provide a rationale
to support the final conclusions.
Elinzanetant is an investigational new drug being evaluated for treatment of vasomotor
symptoms of menopause. Elinzanetant and fezolinetant are neurokinin 1 (NK1) and
neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonists, and fezolinetant was recently approved for
treatment of menopausal symptoms.
Fezolinetant contains a warning in its drug label for potential elevated liver enzymes and
recommends monitoring and follow-up for hepatic function and injury (FDA, 2023). At least one
case of drug-induced liver injury was reported following approval of fezolinetant (NIDDK, 2024).
(b) (4)

Therefore, CTCS was consulted to perform a (Q)SAR assessment of potential hepatobiliary
toxicity for both NK1/3 antagonists and comment on their structural similarities.

Elinzanetant

Fezolinetant

Overall, elinzanetant is predicted to be equivocal for the endpoints of liver damage and
cholestasis, positive for bile duct disorders and gall bladder disorders, and negative for liver
enzyme abnormalities. By contrast, fezolinetant is predicted or reported to be positive for the
endpoints of liver damage, liver enzymes, and gall bladder and negative for cholestasis and bile
duct disorders. Notably, the individual model predictions for elinzanetant for the liver damage
and liver enzyme abnormalities endpoints are generally more negative than for fezolinetant,
while for the endpoints of cholestasis and bile duct disorders the predictions are generally more
positive. However, it is difficult to draw any conclusions about relative hepatotoxicity risk for
elinzanetant compared to fezolinetant because their respective structures have limited
similarity and, with the exception of the fluorobenzene alert, most significant structurally alerting
features identified between the two drugs were different.

1
Reference ID: 5623053

It is noted that elinzanetant and fezolinetant are predicted to be negative and positive,
respectively, for liver enzyme abnormalities by the CU model despite identifying a similar
structural alert corresponding to the bridging bonds between two aryl groups. During expert
review of the predictions it was determined that the alerts are weighted differently for each
molecule because of the dissimilar ring types between the two structures (pyridine-benzene in
elinzanetant; thadiazole-triazole in fezolinetant). Therefore, the (Q)SAR predictions do not
support the conclusion that clinical observations of elevated liver enzymes reported for
fezolinetant should also be expected for elinzanetant.
While it is not possible to determine whether elinzanetant will present the same hepatic adverse
event profile as fezolinetant based on chemical structure, a survey of other structurally similar
analogs outside of the (Q)SAR model training sets identified a more structurally relevant drug,
netupitant, that may serve as a comparator to elinzanetant. Netupitant is also an NK1 receptor
antagonist and shares most of its substructural features with elinzanetant, including the
bis(trifluoromethyl)benzene, dimethyl acetamide, pyridine, and piperazine groups (Figure 1).
Netupitant does not have any drug-induced liver toxicity effects listed in the FDA drug label for
the combination anti-emetic drug product, Akynzeo (FDA, 2018).

bacterial mutagenicity using multiple complementary methodologies). Overall, all seven impurities were

Does elinzanetant have a potential to impact the next-day driving
ability?
Findings on primary and secondary endpoints in the driving study suggest that next-day driving
performance is impaired in some subjects taking single and repeat dose of elinzanetant 120 mg
and 240 mg. The label should mention that there is a potential for next-day residual effects in
some patients taking elinzanetant 120 mg.

Recommendations for the label are provided below:

Ability to Operate Vehicles or Machinery
Driving performance was assessed at 9 hours after bedtime administration of LYNKUET 120 mg
and 240 mg (two times the recommended dose) in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-and
active-controlled, four-period crossover study in 64 healthy women (mean age 52.1 years) using
a computer-based driving simulation. The primary outcome measure was the difference from
placebo in the Standard Deviation of Lateral Position (SDLP). Driving performance was
evaluated using a validated threshold established in a population with blood alcohol
concentration of 0.05%. Although the mean SDLP did not reach the threshold for driving
impairment after administration of LYNKUET 120 or 240 mg, driving ability was impaired in
some subjects taking LYNKUET 120 or 240 mg.

2

Reference ID: 5555516

Background
The next-day driving ability following single dose and multiple doses (120 mg, 240 mg) of
elinzanetant, administered at bedtime, was evaluated in healthy women by assessment of the
mean standard deviation of the lateral position (SDLP) using driving simulator.
Study design
Figure 1 shows the design features of the driving study.
This study was conducted in a single center based on randomized, double-blind, placebo- and
active controlled, 4-fold crossover design with oral administration of multiple doses (over 5
subsequent days) of elinzanetant 120 mg, elinzanetant 240 mg, placebo, or zopiclone 7.5 mg (on
Days 1 and 5 only) per treatment period.
The 120 mg/day dose is the intended therapeutic dose. An additional dose of 240 mg/day was
selected as supratherapeutic dose based on the following reasons. This dose leads to
approximately twice the exposure of the therapeutic dose. The drug exposure of the 240 mg
covers a potential maximum exposure increase of elinzanetant that could occur when
elinzanetant is administered together with a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor as co-medication. The
predicted steady state plasma concentrations have been investigated in healthy participants,
where single elinzanetant doses of up to 600 mg were found to be safe and well tolerated.
Study duration of 5 days was chosen since steady state concentrations would be achieved after 5
days of once daily dosing. Accumulation was expected to be modest (< 2-fold) after multiple
dosing. After 14 days less than 20% receptor NK-1 occupancy was anticipated. This interval was
deemed sufficient to exclude carry-over of pharmacodynamic effects of elinzanetant. NK-1
receptor antagonism is considered as the underlying mechanism of observed somnolence and
fatigue during elinzanetant treatment. Hence, each treatment period was separated by a 7- to 14day washout period.
Study interventions were administered in the evening via oral administration together with 240
mL of non-carbonated water at room temperature. Driving simulator assessments were
performed the next morning, approximately 9-10 hours after dosing. This timing was chosen to
reflect the recommended intake time of elinzanetant according to the intended label and to
investigate potential residual driving impairment and cognitive effects which might pose a risk
for patients. Blood samples for PK analysis were collected pre-dose on Days 1 and 6- and 8.5hours post-dose on Days 2 and 6. The relationship between elinzanetant plasma concentrations
and driving performance was evaluated.
Simulated driving performance was measured using SDLP in the CRCDS-MiniSim™ 9-10h
after dosing. Additional measures of simulated driving performance in the CRCDS-MiniSim™
included Lane Exceedance, Excessive Speed Count, Average Speed and Speed Deviation,
Excessive Ay, Total Collisions, and Divided Attention. Somnolence was measured using the
KSS score.

Analysis methodology
SDLP data was analyzed using a mixed model with fixed effects for sequence, period, and
treatment, with repeated periods for participants. Noninferiority testing was applied, with a
noninferiority margin (NIM) of 4.4 cm. Various comparisons are listed below:
• Noninferiority of clinical dose (120 mg) vs placebo with respect to SDLP mean at day 2.
• Noninferiority of clinical dose (120 mg) vs placebo with respect to SDLP mean at day 6.
• Noninferiority of high dose (240 mg) vs placebo with respect to SDLP mean at day 2.
• Noninferiority of high dose (240 mg) vs placebo with respect to SDLP mean at day 6.
Each test was performed with a significance level of 2.5% one sided. No adjustment to alpha
levels was made for either the comparison of zopiclone to placebo, or for secondary endpoints or
analyses. All tests comparing zopiclone to placebo are only used to assess assay sensitivity.
Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis: Summaries of the correlation of elinzanetant
plasma concentrations and SLDP difference from placebo (SDLP change) were determined.
Also, the relationship between next-day residual concentrations of elinzanetant and SDLP
difference from placebo after single and repeat dose was quantified using a linear regression
model. The mean and 95% CI of the intercepts and slopes were calculated.
Results
Assay Sensitivity
Zopiclone separated from placebo demonstrating assay sensitivity on both Day 2 (Table 1). The
upper limit of 95%CI exceeded 4.4cm threshold on Day 2.
Analysis for primary endpoint
For elinzanetant 120 mg, the upper limits of the 95% CIs of the SDLP differences from placebo
on Day 2 (3.028 cm) and on Day 6 (0.183 cm) did not exceed the pre-established noninferiority
margin (NIM) of 4.4 cm (Figure 2).
For elinzanetant 240 mg, the upper limits of the 95% CIs of the SDLP differences from placebo
on Day 2 (3.116 cm) and on Day 6 (-0.211 cm) did not exceed the pre-established NIM of 4.4
cm. The effect on driving impairment is lower on Day 6 compared to Day 2 likely due to the
development of tolerance (Figure 2, Table 1).

Mutagenic/Genotoxic (y/n/equivocal/na; assay): No.
Elinzanetant tosylate at concentrations up to 1,500 μg/plate (in terms of free base) did
not generate positive mutagenicity signals in AMES assays in the presence or absence

with oral doses up to 2,000 mg/kg/day for 2 days.

Basis for Doses Selected
Per the recommendations of the Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee
(Exec CAC), a high dose of 60 mg/kg/day (30 mg/kg BID) was selected to provide an
AUC > 25-fold higher than the AUC generated by the maximal recommended human
dose (MRHD). The mid- and low-dose were selected based on adequate spacing of
AUCs.
Because elinzanetant is being developed for the clinical indication of moderate to
severe vasomotor symptoms in postmenopausal women, the Exec CAC also suggested
that the carcinogenicity study could be conducted only in female rats.
Prior FDA Exec CAC Dose Concurrence? Yes; October 19, 2020.
In the minutes issued by the Exec CAC following the SPA under IND 129492, the
committee noted that, if the clinical dose changed such that the exposure ratio would no
longer be at least 25-fold at the high dose, the carcinogenicity study would likely be
inadequate to inform risk assessment. As summarized in Table 1, the Applicant used

Rat Carcinogenicity Conclusion: Positive
Rat Tumor Findings (details):
The FDA statistical reviewer Feng Zhou, MS, Division of Biometrics VI, reviewed the
Applicant-submitted tumor data. The reviewer labeled experimental groups 1, 2, 3, 4,
and 5 as VC (Vehicle Control; aqueous solution of 1% methylcellulose (viscosity 400
cP), LD (Low Dose), LM (Low-Mid Dose), MD (Mid Dose), and HD (High Dose),
respectively. The analysis included all the data from all groups to identify statistically
significant dose-response relationships and pairwise comparisons between each test
article-treated group and the control group. Dose-response relationships were
considered statistically significant at p < 0.005 and p < 0.025 for a common tumor and a
rare tumor, respectively. Pairwise comparisons were considered statistically significant
at p < 0.01 and p < 0.05 for a common tumor and a rare tumor, respectively.
As summarized in Table 2, the FDA statistical reviewer identified the following
statistically significant dose-response relationships and pairwise comparisons:
•

Malignant lymphoma in the hematolymphoid system [Common tumor]
o Dose-response relationship p trend = 0.0002
o ↑ Tumor incidence in the HD compared to the VC group (p = 0.0087)

•

Malignant endometrial adenocarcinoma [Common tumor] in uterus
o Dose-response relationship p trend < 0.00001
o ↑ Tumor incidence in the MD and HD compared to VC (p = 0.0006 and
0.00001, respectively)

•

Combined malignant and benign endometrial tumors [Common tumors] in
uterus
o Dose-response relationship p trend < 0.00001
o ↑ Tumor incidence in the MD and HD compared to VC (p = 0.0006 and
0.00001, respectively)

•

Combined malignant and benign endometrial tumors [Common tumors]
and malignant squamous cell carcinoma [Rare tumor] in uterus
o Dose-response relationship p trend < 0.00001
o ↑ Tumor incidence in the MD and HD compared to VC (p = 0.0003 and
0.00001, respectively)

The FDA statistician identified a statistically significant dose-response relationship for
malignant squamous cell carcinoma, a rare tumor, in the uterus (p trend < 0.0206).
However, in the pairwise comparisons, the incidence of this carcinoma did not differ
significantly between test article-treated and VC groups (Table 2).

Systemic Exposures
The low mid-dose of elinzanetant (20 mg/kg/day) was the highest dose not associated
with carcinogenic signals in female rats, and the mid-dose of elinzanetant (60
mg/kg/day) was the lowest dose associated with carcinogenic signals in female rats.
The area-under-the curve 0→24 h (AUC0-24h) generated by each dose on treatment day
358 was 64000 μg•h/L and 252000 μg•h/L, respectively.
Based on statistical modeling of pharmacokinetic data from female VMS patients, the
geometric value of the steady-state AUC0-24h generated by the MRHD of elinzanetant
(120 mg) is 8572 μg•h/L (Clinical Report B002427, Table 21.3.1, Pg 521). Therefore, as
shown in Table 3, based on AUCs, the exposure margins provided by the highest
noncarcinogenic dose and the lowest carcinogenic dose in rats to the MRHD are
approximately 7.5x and 29.4x, respectively.
According to the clinical study CPMX 50130 in which human subjects were given an
oral dose of radiolabeled elinzanetant, BAY3462933 (M30/34) was identified as the
predominant metabolite of the parent drug in humans. M30/34 accounted for
approximately 11% of the total radioactivity recovered from the plasma of elinzanetanttreated subjects. Two other metabolites, BAY3462932 (M27) and BAY3462934
(M18/21), accounted for approximately 6% and 5.5% of the total radioactivity recovered
from the plasma of the study subjects.

Rat Study Comments:
Survival
The survival analyses conducted by the FDA statistical reviewer and by the Applicant
revealed no statistically significant dose-response relationship for mortality. The survival
rates in the VC, LD, LM, MD, or HD groups at the time all rats were terminated on Week
104 were 44%, 39%, 38%, 42%, and 37%, respectively.
Elinzanetant-Related In-Life Findings
Treatment of female rats with elinzanetant resulted in a dose-dependent reduction of
body weight gain. At week 104, female rats in the LD, LM, MD, and HD groups weighed
~9%, 9%, 17%, and 19% less than rats in the VC group.
In a functional observation battery, central nervous system (CNS)-related safety signals
of clinical relevance were also observed at doses ≥60 mg/kg/day, unless otherwise
noted in the list below. These CNS-related safety signals, including convulsions, were
also observed in the pivotal 13-week oral repeat-dose toxicity study in rats (Study No.
RH17GJ).
• Increased incidence and severity of whole-body convulsions. Convulsion was
related to “undetermined” death in several animals at the MD and HD groups.
• Increased incidence of hunched posture.
• Decreased general activity.
• Increased sensitivity to touch.
• Increased salivation.

Elinzanetant-Related Non-Neoplastic Histopathological Findings
The following non-neoplastic histopathological findings were observed at doses ≥60
mg/kg/day, unless otherwise noted:
• Uterus: Squamous cell metaplasia.
• Ovaries: Absence of corpora lutea and increased incidence of sex cord stromal
hyperplasia and granulosa cell hyperplasia.
• Vagina: Decreased mucification.
• Mesenteric lymph node: Increased macrophage infiltrates (at ≥7 mg/kg/day).
• Liver: Biliary hyperplasia, biliary cysts, and multinucleated hepatocytes that
correlated with increased liver weight.
• Adrenal glands: Hyperplasia or hypertrophy of the zona fasciculata, cystic
degeneration, and hypertrophy of the zona glomerulosa in the adrenal cortex that
correlated with increased adrenal weight.
• Parotid salivary gland, lacrimal glands, and pancreas: Atrophy.
Elinzanetant-Associated Reduction of Incidence of Common Spontaneous
Tumors in the Mammary, Thyroid, and Pituitary Glands
Compared to female rats treated with vehicle, female rats treated with elinzanetant
doses ≥60 mg/kg/day presented with reduced occurrence of: (i) hyperplasia in the
mammary gland, (ii) benign thyroid C-cell adenomas, and (iii) adenomas in the pars
distalis of the thyroid gland. Although the Applicant reported that these findings did not
reach statistical significance, they could be related to the ability of the metabolite
M30/34 to inhibit ERα and/or the ability of elinzanetant to decrease the activity of the
hypothalamic-pituitary-gonad axis via inhibition of NK1/NK3 receptors in hypothalamic
KNDy neurons leading to decreased estradiol-promoted cellular proliferation in
estrogen-sensitive organs such as mammary, thyroid, and pituitary glands.

Mouse Carcinogenicity Conclusion: Negative
Mouse Tumor Findings (details):
The tumor data were analyzed by the FDA statistical reviewer,. Feng Zhou, MS,
Division of Biometrics VI, for dose response relationships across the vehicle control
group, and low, mid, and high dose groups, and pairwise comparisons of each of the
three treated groups against the vehicle control group. Two separate analyses were
conducted, one in male mice and one in female mice.
No tumor types with a statistically significant dose response relationship in tumor
incidences were observed in male or female mice with increased elinzanetant dose
when the positive control group was excluded. The pairwise comparisons also showed
no tumor types with a statistically significant increase in tumor incidences in
elinzanetant treated groups, when compared to the vehicle control group in either male
or female mice when the positive control group was excluded.

Margins of exposure compared to human exposure [Total] and human exposure

Elinzanetant:
• The high-dose level of 85 mg/kg/day elinzanetant, in the male mouse has a
corresponding AUC0-24h of 23900 ng•h/mL (Week 26), representing a Multiple of

clinical study B002427].
Metabolites:
Similarly for the metabolites of interest M27, M30/34 and M18/21, the exposure margins
at NOAEL (high dose) were calculated. These metabolites exhibit high affinity and
activity at the human NK1 and NK3 receptors that are similar to the affinity and activity
of elinzanetant in in vitro binding and cellular functional assays. The fraction unbound
values for human and mouse were derived from in-vitro plasma protein binding studies
PH-42081 and PH-42138 and used to calculate unbound exposure for Elinzanetant and
the metabolites, as well as the MoE. These are summarized in the table below:

Reviewer comment: MOE is higher when considering the unbound fraction
based on in-vitro plasma binding.
Mouse Study Comments:
Elinzanetant did not affect the overall survival rate or adverse clinical signs up to the
high dose of 85 mg/kg/day in males and 70 mg/kg/day in females. The survival rates
were 88%, 92%, 96% and 92% for males, and 88%, 100%, 100% and 92% for females,
in the dose groups 0 (vehicle), 10, 30 and 85 mg/kg/day for males and dose groups 0
(vehicle), 10, 20 and 70 mg/kg/day for females, respectively. No elinzanetant-related
changes in body weight, body weight gain, or food consumption were observed over the
course of the 26-week study.
No non-neoplastic findings related to elinzanetant were identified.
Questions to the Exec CAC:
1. In a clinical PK study, the Applicant identified M30/34 as the predominant metabolite
in humans (accounting for ~11% of the total radioactivity recovered from the plasma
of [3H]elinzanetant-treated human subjects). The Applicant identified two other
metabolites, M27 and M18/21, each of which accounted for ~6% and 5.5%,
respectively, of the total radioactivity recovered from the plasma of the same study
subjects. While the rat study provides reasonable multiples of exposure for the
primary metabolite M30/34, it provides very low multiples of exposure for M27 and
M18/21. Given that neither metabolite exceeds 10% of the metabolite profile in
humans, would we consider the rat carcinogenicity study adequate to inform the
carcinogenic potential of elinzanetant?
2. In the mouse study, the Applicant took into account the percent (%) of protein
unbound fraction to estimate multiples of exposure. The % unbound fraction was
derived from an in-vitro study, as summarized in Table 4. Would this approach be
acceptable?
Post eCAC meeting notes:
1. The Exec CAC agreed metabolite coverage in rat carcinogenicity study is
adequate.

Pharmacology/ Toxicology Summary
Pharmacology (primary & MoA)
Key Findings:
Elinzanetant is a dual NK-1 and NK-3 receptor (NK-1R and NK-3R) antagonist and
displays high affinity for human NK-1 receptors [pKi values of 8.71 – 10.15 (mean pKi of
9.43)] and NK-3 receptors [pKi values of 8.03 – 8.8 (mean pKi of 8.42)], leading to an
~10-fold lower affinity of elinzanetant towards human NK3 receptors compared to
human NK1 receptors. Strong antagonism at human NK-1R and NK-3R, with calculated
pKB values of 9.02 - 9.1 (human NK-1 receptor) and 8.17 - 8.5 (human NK-3 receptor)
was demonstrated for elinzanetant in functional in-vitro assays.
• Based on radioligand binding displacement assays, elinzanetant has relatively
higher selectivity to NK-1R and NK-3R subtypes than the NK-2R subtype of
different species, including humans, baboons, gerbils, guinea pigs, and rats.
o Rat NK receptors are generally less sensitive to elinzanetant than the
human receptors.
• Based on in-vitro functional assays, elinzanetant acts as an insurmountable
antagonist at NK1 and NK3 receptors.
Mechanism of Action: NK receptors are Gq protein coupled receptors expressed by
KNDy neurons in the infundibular nucleus of the thalamus in humans. KNDy neurons
synapse onto neurons in the vasomotor center in the hypothalamic median preoptic
nucleus and onto GnRH-expressing neurons in the infundibular nucleus and the
preoptic nucleus. NK receptor activation in KNDy neurons stimulates vasomotor
responses. It also stimulates the release of GnRH that stimulates the anterior pituitary
gland to secrete luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) that, in
turn, can increase secretion of sex hormones from the gonads.
In the context of vasomotor symptoms in postmenopausal women, NK-3R antagonists
are thought to act by inhibiting the activity of KNDy neurons, thereby suppressing the
activation of the vasomotor center.
Metabolites:
The principal metabolites of interest (M27, M30/34 and M18/21), which accounted for
6%, 11% and 5.5% respectively of total radioactivity in a human clinical study (# CPMX
50130), each showed high affinity and antagonistic activity at the human NK-1R and
NK-3R similar to the affinity and activity of elinzanetant at human NK-1R and NK-3R.
The binding affinity and functional antagonism of elinzanetant and its metabolites at
human NK-1R and NK-3R are noted in Table 5.

Pharmacokinetics
Key Findings:
In rat, following an oral dose, clearance was low and plasma elimination terminal halflife of the unchanged compound was long with 6.3 and 7.8 h in male and female rat.
Elinzanetant was brain penetrant in the rat and monkey with brain to blood ratios of 0.1
to 0.2 and 0.6, respectively.
Plasma Protein Binding: The plasma protein binding of elinzanetant was high in male
and female human plasma, in female SD rat plasma, and in female Cynomolgus
monkey plasma and resulted in a low fraction unbound (fu) of less than 1%. The protein
binding in female and male CD-1 mouse plasma and in male SD rat plasma was noted
to be lower, with fu values of approximately 2-3%. Similar plasma protein binding
profiles were identified for the main human metabolites, M27, M30/34, and M18/21, as
shown in Tables 6 through 9.

Genotoxicity
Key Findings:
A full battery of genotoxicity studies including an AMES test, an in-vitro mouse
lymphoma L5178Y cell assay, and an in-vivo rat micronucleus assay did not reveal any
evidence of a genotoxic potential of elinzanetant.
Carcinogenicity
Key Findings:
104-week carcinogenicity study in female Sprague Dawley rat (Study T105128-7):
•
•

•

Oral treatment of female rats with elinzanetant doses ranging from 7 to 80
mg/kg/day compared to vehicle for 104 weeks reduced their body weight gain but
had no effect on their survival.
Neoplastic Histopathology:
o Elinzanetant caused statistically significant increases in the incidence of
malignant adenocarcinoma of the uterus and malignant lymphoma in the
hematolymphoid system.
o Elinzanetant also caused statistically significant increases in the incidence
of combined uterine adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma.
o The oral dose of 20 mg/kg/day was the highest test dose not associated
with carcinogenic signals in female rats. Based on AUCs, the clinical
exposure margins provided by the highest noncarcinogenic dose to the
MRHD is ~7.5x for elinzanetant and ~0.2x, 3.7x, and 0.05x for the
metabolites M27, M30/34, and M18/21, respectively.
o The oral dose of 60 mg/kg/day was the lowest test dose associated with
carcinogenic signals in female rats. Based on AUCs, the clinical exposure
margin provided by this dose to the MRHD is ~29.4x for elinzanetant and
~0.8x, 7.0x, and 0.1x for the metabolites M27, M30/34, and M18/21,
respectively.
Elinzanetant-related, non-neoplastic findings included:
o Squamous cell metaplasia in the uterus (≥60 mg/kg/day).
o Biliary hyperplasia, biliary cysts, and multinucleated hepatocytes that
correlated with increased liver weight. Biliary hyperplasia and increased
incidence of biliary cysts correlated with the increased bilirubin
concentration (≥60 mg/kg/day).
o Epithelial hyperplasia (≥7 mg/kg/day) and decreased lymphocyte counts
(≥20 mg/kg/day) in the thymus that correlated with decreased thymus
weight.
o Absence of corpora lutea, sex cord stromal hyperplasia, and granulosa
cell hyperplasia in the ovaries (≥60 mg/kg/day).
o Increased macrophage infiltrates in the mesenteric lymph node (≥7
mg/kg/day).
o Hyperplasia or hypertrophy of the zona fasciculata, cystic degeneration,
and hypertrophy of the zona glomerulosa in the adrenal cortex that
correlated with increased adrenal weight (≥60 mg/kg/day).

Nonclinical Assessment and Recommendation
Under NDA 219469, Bayer Healthcare Pharmaceuticals, Inc., is developing
elinzanetant, an NK-1R/NK-3R antagonist, for the clinical indication of treatment of
moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause.
The Applicant has conducted a 2-year carcinogenicity study in female rats treated by
oral gavage with elinzanetant doses ranging from 7 to 80 mg/kg/day. They have also
conducted a 26-week carcinogenicity study in transgenic mice treated by oral gavage
with doses ranging from 10 to 85 mg/kg/day for male mice and 10 to 70 mg/kg/day for
female mice.
The data analysis by the FDA statistical reviewer and the Applicant led to the
conclusions that: (i) in transgenic male and female mice, elinzanetant did not induce
statistically significant neoplastic or non-neoplastic findings, and (ii) elinzanetant was
carcinogenic in female rats.
In female rats, elinzanetant significantly increased the incidence of malignant lymphoma
in the hematolymphoid system and malignant endometrial adenocarcinoma. The dose
response-relationships for elinzanetant-induced increased incidence of these common
tumors were statistically significant at p < 0.005, and pairwise comparisons were
significant between rats treated with elinzanetant doses ≥60 mg/kg/day and vehicle
control (p < 0.01). The highest noncarcinogenic dose was 20 mg/kg/day.
Elinzanetant significantly increased the incidence of combined malignant and benign
endometrial tumors and malignant squamous cell carcinoma in uterus. The effects were

18
Reference ID: 5523839

NDA # 219469

Reviewers: Edna De Fatima Albuquerque, PhD
Pratistha Tamrakar, PhD
Sarah Lee, PhD

statistically significant with respect to the dose-response relationships and pairwise
group comparisons with VC at doses ≥60 mg/kg/day.
Although the dose-response relationship for the rare malignant squamous cell
carcinoma in the uterus was statistically significant (p trend < 0.025), pairwise
comparisons indicated that the incidence of this carcinoma alone did not differ
significantly between elinzanetant- and vehicle-treated female rats.
In-life central nervous system-related safety signals of clinical relevance were observed
during the functional observation battery recorded during the treatment of the female
rats with elinzanetant. These signals included: (i) whole-body convulsions at doses ≥60
mg/kg/day, and (ii) increased incidence of hunched posture, decreased general activity,
increased sensitivity to touch, and increased salivation at doses ≥60 mg/kg/day.
The following non-neoplastic findings were also observed at doses ≥60 mg/kg/day,
unless otherwise noted in the: (i) liver: biliary hyperplasia, biliary cysts, and
multinucleated hepatocytes that correlated with increased liver weight and increased
serum bilirubin levels; (ii) uterus: squamous cell metaplasia; (ii) ovaries: absence of
corpora lutea and increased incidence of sex cord stromal hyperplasia and granulosa
cell hyperplasia; (iv) vagina: decreased mucification; (v) mesenteric lymph node:
increased macrophage infiltrates (at ≥7 mg/kg/day); (v) adrenal glands: hyperplasia or
hypertrophy of the zona fasciculata, cystic degeneration, and hypertrophy of the zona
glomerulosa in the adrenal cortex that correlated with increased adrenal weight; and
(vii) parotid salivary gland, lacrimal glands, and pancreas: atrophy.
Although not discussed in the Applicant’s report, the main metabolites of elinzanetant –
BAY 3462932 (M27), BAY 3462933 (M30/34), and BAY 346934 (M18/21) – inhibit
[3H]progesterone binding to PR-B with Kis of 1.08 μM, 0.96 μM, and 1.35 μM,
respectively. Elinzanetant does not interact with PR-B. Considering that, in female rats
treated with the elinzanetant dose of 60 mg/kg/day, Cmax and AUC0-24h of BAY 3462933
(M30/34) were 2.09 μM and 46.8 μM•h, respectively, on treatment day 358, it is possible
that inhibition of PR-B by BAY 3462933 (M30/34) contributes to the increased incidence
of endometrial cancers in rats treated with elinzanetant doses ≥60 mg/kg/day.
At 10 μM, BAY 3462933 (M30/34) has been reported to inhibit by ~60% and ~55%
radioligand binding to ERα ectopically expressed in Sf9 cells and to GABAA receptors in
rat brain membranes, respectively. BAY 3462933 (M30/34)-induced inhibition of ERα
activity could contribute to the reduced incidence of tumors and hyperplasia in estradiolsensitive organs (such as the mammary, pituitary, and thyroid glands) in elinzanetanttreated female rats. BAY 3462933 (M30/34)-induced inhibition of PR-B and GABAA
receptors could also contribute to the proconvulsant effects of elinzanetant in female
rats.
Based on trend and pairwise comparisons, the FDA statistical reviewer and the
Applicant concluded that, in female rats, the highest noncarcinogenic dose was 20
mg/kg/day (which provide a clinical exposure margin of ~7.5x) and the lowest

1 Background
1.1 Regulatory History
Under NDA 219469, the Applicant, Bayer Healthcare Pharmaceuticals, Inc., is
developing elinzanetant, an NK1/NK3 receptor antagonist, for the clinical indication of
treatment of moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause.
Clinical and nonclinical studies to support the advanced development of elinzanetant
were conducted under IND 129492.
On August 14, 2020, the Applicant submitted to IND 129492 a request for a Rat
Carcinogenicity Study Special Protocol Assessment (SPA). After being initially rejected
due to lack of a signed full report of the nonclinical repeat-dose toxicity study used to
support the proposed dose selection for the carcinogenic study, the study protocol for
the rat carcinogenic study was resubmitted on September 4, 2020 [IND 129492, SDN
34, SN 0033]. The SPA Agreement for the Rat Carcinogenicity Study from the Division
and the FDA’s Exec CAC was provided to the Sponsor on October 19, 2020.
On October 24, 2022, the Applicant submitted to IND 129492 an SPA for a mouse
TgRasH2 carcinogenicity study. The SPA Agreement for the Mouse Carcinogenicity
Study from the Division and the FDA’s Exec CAC was provided to the Sponsor on
December 8, 2022. The Applicant opened the NDA on July 26, 2024, and submitted the
results of the rat carcinogenic study T105128-7 to both the NDA and the IND.
1.2 Relevant INDs, NDAs, BLAs or DMFs
IND 129492. Drug: Elinzanetant; Sponsor: Bayer Healthcare Pharmaceuticals, Inc.;
Indication: Treatment of moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms
associated with menopause; IND Submission Date: February 04, 2016.

Positive
Key Study Findings
Long-term carcinogenicity studies were conducted in rats dosed orally with
elinzanetant for 104 weeks. Female rats were dosed at 0, 7, 20, 60, and 80 mg/kg/day.
In female rats, elinzanetant was found to be carcinogenic at doses ≥60 mg/kg, which
generated systemic exposures (AUC0-24h) ≥29.4-fold higher than the human systemic
exposure at the MRHD of 120 mg/day.
Adequacy of Carcinogenicity Study
• Adequate multiples of the clinical exposure were achieved in the carcinogenicity
study in rats (29.4x and 32.8x for the mid-dose and the high-dose groups,
respectively).

Survival to scheduled necropsy was greater than 40% in all groups (with >20 rats
surviving until terminal sacrifice at Week 104), without a clear dose-related
mortality.
Body weight gain was reduced dose dependently in female rats treated with
elinzanetant.
o At terminal sacrifice, body weights of female rats in the LD, LM, MD, and

of female rats in the VC group.
o The reduced body weight gain was not due to reduced feed consumption.

Appropriateness of Test Models
The carcinogenicity study in rats appears appropriate because:
• Animals received treatment through the entire duration of the study (104 weeks).
• Although the study was restricted to female rats, the drug is being develop for a
clinical indication in women.
• The rat strain (Sprague-Dawley) was the same as that used in the repeat-dose
toxicity study that served as the basis for the selection of test doses.
Evaluation of Tumor Findings
• The FDA statistical reviewer Feng Zhou reported:
o Statistically significant increase in the incidence of malignant lymphoma in

pairwise comparisons between doses ≥60 mg/kg/day and VC.
o Statistically significant increase of combined malignant and benign

doses ≥60 mg/kg/day and VC.

squamous cell carcinoma in the uterus at the level of the dose-response
relationship but not at the level of pairwise comparisons.

Causes of Early Morbidity and Mortality: Causes of early morbidity and mortality are
presented in Table 14.
Common causes of death/moribund condition for female rats at an unscheduled time
included mammary gland neoplasms and pituitary adenoma of the pars distalis,
particularly in the VC, LD, and ML dose groups (Table 14). These are representative of
common, spontaneously occurring, age-related findings in laboratory rats.
Causes of early deaths among female rats that received elinzanetant doses ≥60
mg/kg/day included: (i) an increased incidence of malignant lymphoma and uterine
neoplasms, and (ii) an increased incidence of an “undetermined” cause of death, largely
related to clinical observations of convulsions. Due to lack of microscopic correlates in
the brain, the Applicant refers to convulsions-associated deaths as deaths of
“undetermined cause”.
It was also noted that in the MD and HD groups, the incidence of mammary gland
neoplasms-associated deaths decreased.

Reviewer’s Comment on Biological Plausibility of Elinzanetant-Induced
Convulsions
Considering the current knowledge that NK1 and NK3 receptor activation
increases neuronal excitability,1,2 it is unlikely that elinzanetant-induced inhibition
of NK1/NK3 receptors would lead to the development of convulsions.
The Applicant has reported that, at 10 μM, the elinzanetant metabolite BAY
3462933 (M30/34) inhibits by ~55% [3H]tert-butylbicycloorthobenzoate
([3H]TBOB) binding to gamma-amino butyric acid type A (GABAA) receptors in
Wistar rat brain membrane preparations (R-14018). Since GABAA receptor
antagonists (e.g., picrotoxin and bicuculline) are well known for their
proconvulsant effects,3 BAY 3462933 (M30/34)-induced inhibition of GABAA
receptors may contribute to the proconvulsant effects of elinzanetant in rats. It is
also possible that BAY 3462933 (M30/34)-induced PR-B inhibition contributes to
the proconvulsant properties of elinzanetant because progesterone receptor
antagonists and null mutations of the genes that encode progesterone receptors
A and B reportedly suppress the anticonvulsant effects of progesterone.4,5
Ophthalmological examinations performed on main study animals in Weeks 7, 26, 52,
and 100 revealed no elinzanetant-related abnormal ophthalmological findings.
Body Weights
Body weight was recorded at least once before treatment, once daily between treatment
days 1 and 15, once weekly thereafter until treatment day 134, once every four weeks
after day 134 followed by once every two weeks starting on day 246 until the end of
treatment.
Treatment with elinzanetant dose dependently reduced the body weight gain of female
rats (Figure 2). The reduction in body weight gain was not due to a reduction in food
consumption, which was not significantly different between treatment groups.

Neoplastic Findings
FDA Statistical Analysis of Tumor Findings
The FDA statistical reviewer Feng Zhou conducted an independent review of the
Applicant’s report data (for details regarding the method and data analysis, refer to the
FDA Statistical Review of Feng Zhou in Appendix 1).
In short, the statistical reviewer used the Poly-k method described in Bailer and Portier
(1988) and Bieler and Williams (1993) to analyze the tumor data from the five test
groups (VC, LD, LM, MD, and HD) to identify statistically significant dose-response
relationships and pairwise comparisons between test article groups and the VC group.
To adjust for the effect of multiple testing, the statistical reviewer used the
methodologies described in the Draft Guidance: Statistical Aspects of the Design,
Analysis, and Interpretation of Chronic Rodent Carcinogenicity Studies of
Pharmaceuticals (2001), available at https://www.fda.gov/media/72296/download. Per
the Guidance, criteria for identification of statistically significant effects in 2-year
carcinogenicity studies with 50 rats/group were as follows:
• Dose-response relationships were considered statistically significant at α = 0.025 for
rare tumors (i.e., tumors with a background rate of ≤1%) and α = 0.005 for common
tumors.
• Pairwise comparisons between each test article group and control were considered
statistically significant at α = 0.05 for rare tumors and α = 0.01 for common tumors.
Summary of the FDA Statistical Reviewer’s Neoplastic Findings in Female Rats
Uterus
The FDA statistical reviewer identified statistically significant positive dose-response
relationships for elinzanetant-related neoplastic findings in the female rat uterus, with an
increase in the incidence of malignant endometrial adenocarcinomas (a common tumor)
and of combined benign and malignant endometrial cancers (common tumors) and
malignant endometrial squamous cell carcinoma (a rare tumor) (trend; p-values <
0.0001). The incidence of these tumors was higher in female rats treated with the oral
elinzanetant doses of 60 mg/kg/day and 80 mg/kg/day compared to concurrent vehicle
control (pairwise; p-values < 0.006) (Table 2). Both findings meet the recommended

Reviewer’s Comments
1. Based on the FDA statistical reviewer’s and the Applicant’s data analyses,
uterine tumors (malignant adenocarcinomas and for the combination of
malignant and benign uterine tumors and malignant squamous cell
carcinoma) and malignant lymphoma in the hematolymphoid system were
considered positive tumor findings due to statistical significance by both
trend and pairwise comparison.
2. The inhibition of PR-B receptors by the elinzanetant metabolite M30/34
provides a mechanistic basis to support that these tumors are indeed
elinzanetant-treatment related (See Biological Plausibility section below).
This reviewer agrees that the tumor findings in the uterus and the
hematolymphoid system are due to the elinzanetant treatment.
3. Biological Plausibility of Elinzanetant-Related Carcinogenic Signals in Rats
According to the results of binding studies in the nonclinical reports R14017, R-14018, and R-14019, the main elinzanetant metabolites – BAY
3462932 (M27), BAY 3462933 (M30/34), and BAY 346934 (M18/21) – inhibit
[3H]progesterone binding to the progesterone receptor B isoform (PR-B)
ectopically expressed in human T-47D cells with Kis of approximately 1.08
μM, 0.96 μM, and 1.35 μM, respectively. Elinzanetant itself does not interact
with PR-B.
BAY 3462933 (M30/34) is the most abundant metabolite of elinzanetant in
rats and humans. The toxicokinetic assessments conducted as part of the
carcinogenicity study in rats revealed that Cmax and AUC0-24h of BAY
3462933 (M30/34) in rats treated with the elinzanetant dose of 60 mg/kg/day
were 1430 μg/L (~2.1 μM, considering that the molecular weight attributed
to the metabolite is ~685.3) and 32100 μg•h/L (~46.8 μM•h), respectively, on
treatment day 358. These concentrations would be sufficient to inhibit by
>50% the activity of PR-Bs.
Since progesterone-induced PR-B activation is known to suppress
proliferation of epithelial and stromal cells in the endometrium6 and loss of
PR-B has been associated with development of invasive endometrial

cancer in humans,7 it is possible that PR-B inhibition by BAY 3462933

endometrial cancer in rats treated with elinzanetant doses ≥60 mg/kg/day.
Although less is known about the role of PR-B receptors in lymphomas, it
has been reported that progesterone can suppress the proliferation of Tand B-lymphoma cell lines.8 If the antiproliferative effects of progesterone
on lymphoma cells are mediated by PR-B signaling, BAY 3462933 (M30/34)induced PR-B inhibition could also contribute to the increased incidence of
malignant lymphoma in the hematolymphoid system of elinzanetant-treated
female rats.
Elinzanetant-Associated Reduction of Incidence of Common Spontaneous
Tumors in the Mammary, Thyroid, and Pituitary Glands
Compared to concurrent vehicle control female rats, the groups of female rats treated
with elinzanetant doses ≥60 mg/kg/day presented with lower incidence of: (i) malignant
adenocarcinoma, benign adenoma, benign fibroadenoma, and physiological and
atypical hyperplasia in the mammary glands, (ii) adenomas in the pars distalis of the
pituitary glands, and (iii) benign C-cell adenomas in the thyroid glands (Table 21).
However, the magnitude of the effects did not reach statistical significance.

Reviewer’s Comment on Biological Plausibility of Apparent Reduction of
Incidence of Histopathological Signals of Benign and Malignant Neoplasm
in the Mammary Glands, Pituitary, and Thyroid Glands in Rats
According to a nonclinical pharmacological study, BAY 3462933 (M30/34) at
10 μM inhibited by ~60% binding of [3H]estradiol to human estrogen
receptor α (ERα) ectopically expressed in Sf9 cells (R-14018).
There are several reports that ERα activation can promote hyperplasia and
tumor development in the mammary, thyroid, and pituitary glands.9,10,11
Therefore, in rats treated with elinzanetant doses ≥60 mg/kg/day, BAY
3462933 (M30/34)-induced inhibition of ERα could contribute to the reduced
incidence of: (i) mammary gland neoplasms and hyperplasia, (ii) pituitary
adenomas, and (iii) thyroid C-cell adenomas.

NK1/NK3 receptors are expressed in hypothalamic KNDy
(Kisspeptin/Neurokinin B [NKB]/Dynorphin) neurons, and activation of
these receptors in KNDy neurons increases the activity of gonadotropinreleasing hormone (GnRH)-expressing neurons that, in turn, stimulates the
anterior pituitary gland to release gonadotrophins that induce the release
of sex hormones from the gonads. Elinzanetant-induced inhibition of
NK1/NK3 receptors may lead to a reduction of estradiol levels that could
contribute to the apparent reduction of tumors and hyperplasia in estradiolsensitive organs, including the mammary, pituitary, and thyroid glands.

Toxicokinetics
Blood samples for TK analysis were collected on treatment days 1, 176, 358, and 694
from the satellite animals at different time points after treatment on each day. The TK
parameters of day 694 are only rough estimates because of the sampling scheme and
are not used to estimate clinical exposure margins.
On all test days, systemic exposures to the parent compound elinzanetant and its
metabolites BAY3462932 (M27), BAY3462933 (M30/34), and BAY3462934 (M18/21)
increased as the oral gavage dose of the parent compound increased from 7 to 80
mg/kg/day (Table 27). The metabolites BAY3462932 and BAY3462933 were
quantifiable in blood from animals treated with all doses of elinzanetant on days 1, 176,
358, and 694. Metabolite BAY3462934 was quantifiable in blood from animals treated
with elinzanetant doses ≥20 mg/kg/day on days 1, 176, 358, and 694 and in blood from
animals treated with the low dose of 7 mg/kg/day on days 176, 358, and 694.
As shown in Table 27, exposures to the metabolites were markedly lower than the
exposure to the unchanged parent drug. In agreement with previous pharmacokinetic
studies, metabolite BAY3462933 (M30/34) is the most prevalent in elinzanetant-treated
rats (as it is in humans treated with elinzanetant).

Key Study Findings
There were no statistically significant neoplastic findings related to elinzanetant (BAY
3427080).
No BAY 3427080-related non-neoplastic lesions were observed.
Adequacy of Carcinogenicity Study
The Division considers the transgenic mouse study an adequate assessment of
carcinogenic potential because the high dose of BAY 3427080 was based on MTD and
doses recommended by the Exec CAC were utilized. A single intraperitoneal dose of Nmethyl-N-nitrosourea (MNU) at 75 mg/kg/day was used as a positive control.
The decrease in survival and occurrence of MNU-related findings of neoplasia (such as
malignant lymphomas in the hematolymphoid system, squamous cell papilloma and/or
adenoma in the nonglandular stomach and skin/subcutis) were consistent with the
published literature for the rasH2 transgenic mice administered MNU, validating the
model for this study.
Tables 7A and 7B (pages 72-73) in the appended statistical report summarize the
findings of the analysis conducted by the FDA statistical reviewer for tumor rates and pvalues for dose-response relationship trends and for pairwise comparisons between
vehicle control mice and elinzanetant-treated mice or positive control mice.

Sponsor notes that this finding was considered not related to BAY 3427080 because it
was a single papilloma in the perianal region limited to one female (Animal M0812)
administered 70 mg/kg/day; no corresponding progression for other proliferative or
neoplastic findings (e.g., epidermal hyperplasia or carcinoma, respectively) was noted in
females or males (the latter of which were administered a higher dose of 85 mg/kg/day);
and the tumor in this female was noted macroscopically at the perianal region, a typical
site of chronic grooming (e.g., ano-urogenital region, ears, nose, etc.) for which
cutaneous squamous cell papilloma is documented to occur spontaneously in
transgenic mice (Mecklenburg, et al., 2013)12.
Reviewer Comment: Based on the FDA Statistical reviewer’s assessment,
the neoplastic finding of squamous cell papilloma in the skin/subcutis
[benign] observed in one female administered HD (70 mg/kg/day) was not
statistically significant by trend or pairwise tests as compared to the
concurrent vehicle control group.
Non-Neoplastic
No non-neoplastic findings related to BAY 3427080 were identified.
The Applicant noted microscopic findings of minimal or slight myocyte
degeneration/regeneration, sometimes accompanied by mononuclear and/or mixed cell
infiltrates, in the biceps femoris muscle of almost all animals from all groups, including
concurrent controls (vehicle and positive control groups), was consistent with the
spontaneously occurring skeletal muscle myopathy reported for this transgenic mouse
strain (Tsuchiya et al., 2002).13

Toxicokinetics
In the toxicokinetics analysis, the systemic exposure to BAY 3427080 and its major
metabolites, M27, M30/34, M18/21, was demonstrated.
• In male mice, BAY 3427080 exposure increased moderately more than doseproportionally from 10 to 30 mg/kg/day in terms of AUC0-24h and Cmax, while from
30 to 85 mg/kg/day AUC0-24h and Cmax increased about dose-proportionally.
• In female mice, BAY 3427080 exposure increased slightly more than doseproportionally from 10 to 20 mg/kg/day in terms of AUC0-24h and markedly more
than dose proportional for Cmax; while from 20 to 70 mg/kg/day AUC0-24h and Cmax
increased moderately more than dose-proportional and about dose-proportional,
respectively.

Summary

This review evaluates statistically the data of a 2-year oral carcinogenicity study in female
Sprague-Dawley rats and a 26-weeks oral carcinogenicity study in male and female Hemizygous
rasH2 Transgenic mice. The review analyzes the dose-response relationship of tumor
incidences and mortality (including tumor-related mortality).
Rat Study: One hundred female rats per group (100/group) were dosed by oral gavage with
NT-814 twice daily for up to 104 weeks. The respective NT-814 doses in the vehicle control
(VC), low (LD), mid-low (ML), mid-high (MH), and high (HD) groups were 0, 7, 20, 60, and 80
mg/kg/day. The vehicle control item was 1% aqueous methylcellulose.
The survival analyses didn’t show any statistically significant dose response relationship in
mortality. The female rats were terminated at Week 104. The respective survival rates in the
VC, LD, ML, MH, or HD groups at the time they were terminated were 44%, 39%, 38%, 42%,
and 37%.
The tumor analysis showed that a positive dose response was statistically significant in the
common tumor incidences of malignant lymphoma in hematolymphoid system
(p=0.0020<0.005). For this tumor type, the incidences rate of HD group was statistically
significantly greater than that of the VC group (p=0.0087<0.01). A positive dose response was
statistically significant in the common tumor incidences of malignant adenocarcinoma
endometrium and the combined tumor incidences of benign and malignant endometrium, and
malignant squamous cell in uterus (Ps<0.00001 <0.005). For these tumor types, the incidences
rates of MH and HD groups were statistically significantly greater than that of the VC group
(Ps<0.006<0.01). A positive dose response was statistically significant in the rare tumor
incidences of malignant carcinoma squamous cell in uterus (Ps<0.0206 <0.025). For this
tumor type, the incidence rate in any dosed group was not statistically significantly greater
than that of the vehicle control group.

Mouse Study: Twenty-five mice per sex per group (25/sex/group) were dosed by oral gavage
with NT-814 for up to 26 weeks. The respective NT-814 doses in the vehicle control (VC), low
(LD), mid (MD), high-dose (HD) groups were 0, 10, 30, 85 mg/kg/day for male mice and 0,
10, 20, 70 mg/kg/day female mice. Twenty mice of the positive control (PC) group
(10/sex/group) were dosed with one intraperitoneal dose of N-methyl-N-nitrosourea on day 1
of the dosing phase.
Excluding the PC group, the survival analyses didn’t show any statistically significant dose
response relationship in mortality in males and females. The respective survival rates in the VC,
LD, MD, HD, and PC groups at the time they were terminated were 88%, 92%, 96%, 92%,
and 10% in males and 88%, 100%, 100%, 92%, and 20% in females. The mortality rates for the
PC group were statistically significantly higher than that for the VC group for both male and
female mice.
Excluding the PC group, the tumor analysis showed that there were no statistically significant
positive dose response relationships in any tumor types among the NT-814 treated groups
and the VC group for male and female mice.

Background

The sponsor, Bayer Healthcare Pharmaceuticals, Inc., is submitting a New Drug Application
(NDA) 219469 for Elinzanetant (BAY 3427080, NT814) capsule for the treatment of moderate
to severe vasomotor symptoms (VMS) associated with menopause. The sponsor submitted two
carcinogenicity study reports: Study t105128-7: “A 104-Week Twice Daily Oral Gavage
Toxicokinetic and Carcinogenicity Study with NT-814 (BAY3427080) in Sprague Dawley Rats”
and Study t105265-9: “A 26-Week Carcinogenicity and Toxicokinetic Study of BAY 3427080
(NT-814) When Administered Twice Daily via Oral Gavage to Transgenic Mice”. Study
reports and electronic tumor.xpt and SEND datasets were submitted on 7/26/2024 (via NDA
219469/S-0001.
The phrase "dose response relationship" refers to the linear component of the effect of
treatment, and not necessarily to a strictly increasing or decreasing mortality or tumor incidence
rate as dose increases. Results of this review have been discussed with the nonclinical team.

3

Rat Study- t105128-7

Study Report:
SAS data:

t105128-7-pre-clinical-study-report.pdf (statistical report on page 6700)
Tumor.xpt

The objective of this study was to evaluate the carcinogenic potential and toxicokinetics of NT814 (also known as BAY3427080 and elinzanetant) when administered twice daily (6 hours ±
30 minutes) via oral gavage to female Sprague Dawley (Hsd:Sprague Dawley SD) rats for at
least 104 weeks. Female rats were assigned to five groups, and doses were administered as
indicated in the following table. Animals were dosed via oral gavage at a volume of 5
mL/kg/dose (10 mL/kg/day). The vehicle control item was 1% aqueous methylcellulose.

Assessment of carcinogenicity was based on anatomic pathology to include incidences of
masses or tumors and possible effects on survival. Mortality, clinical observations, body
weight, and food consumption were also monitored and evaluated.

Reference ID: 5523839
5494197

3.1

Page 6 of 22

Sponsor’s Analyses
3.1.1

Survival Analysis

Tests to compare survival were performed, with a two-sided risk for increasing and
decreasing mortality with dose. Tests were performed for dose response (vehicle control and
treated groups only) and for each treated group against vehicle control using Kaplan-Meier
product-limit estimation curves, along with log-rank and Wilcoxon tests. These were
performed using the LIFETEST procedure in SAS. The time to death or sacrifice (in weeks)
was the dependent variable. The treatment group was included as the stratum. Animals with
a death or sacrifice status recorded as a planned terminal sacrifice or an accidental death
were censored in the analysis.
time to death (weeks) =integer part of ([day of death - 1] / 7) + 1).
Sponsor’s concluded results: No NT-814-related effects on survival were noted.
3.1.2

Tumor Data Analysis

Only tumors from tissues listed in the protocol to be examined for all animals were analyzed.
Statistical analysis was performed for each given tumor type. Tests to compare tumor
incidence were performed, with a one-sided risk for increasing incidence with dose. Tests
were performed for dose response (vehicle control and treated groups only) and for each
treated group against vehicle control.
For tumors occurring in animals dying spontaneously or sacrificed in a moribund condition,
the Pathologist classified the context of observation as one of the following:
1. Fatal: The tumor was a factor in the demise of the animal.
2. Non-fatal: The tumor was not a factor in the demise of the animal.
3. Uncertain
Tumors (palpable and non-palpable) were analyzed by the IARC asymptotic fixed intervalbased prevalence test (Peto et al., 1980). The cut off points for the interval-based test were
Weeks 0 to 52, 53 to 78, 79 to 92, 93 to before terminal sacrifice, and the terminal sacrifice.
Fatal and non-fatal tumors were analyzed together, with a separate stratum for each. No
tumors of uncertain context were noted. The test was implemented using PROC
MULTTEST in the SAS system. In the case of sparse tables, the exact form of the test was
used for that stratum. Otherwise, the asymptotic version of the test was used.
Animals were assigned to the terminal sacrifice stratum based on the death or sacrifice status
recorded in the data and were not assigned based on their week of necropsy. Unadjusted Pvalues were reported for tumors. Indication of a possible treatment effect were assessed on
the basis of rare or common tumor type, in line with the FDA guidelines (Food and Drug
Administration Draft Guidance for Industry, 2001). The Study Pathologist determined
whether a tumor type was rare or common.
File Name: NDA219469Carcin

Reference ID: 5523839
5494197

NDA 219469 ● Elinzanetant (NT-814) ● Bayer Pharmaceuticals Inc. ● Carcinogenicity Study

Page 7 of 22

Site or tumor combinations were also statistically analyzed. The criteria for combination
were based on Guidelines for combining neoplasms for evaluation of rodent carcinogenicity
studies (McConnell et al., 1986) and as indicated by the Study Pathologist. Incidences of
multiple-organ and combined neoplastic findings, such as hemangioma, fibrosarcoma, and
endometrial stromal polyp, were counted by animal, not tissue type.
Sponsor’s concluded results: NT-814-related neoplastic findings were noted in the uterus
and hematolymphoid system. These findings included statistically significant increases in the
incidences of uterine neoplasms (adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma) and an
increased severity/incidence of cystic glandular hyperplasia of the endometrium with
concomitant, but not statistically significant, endometrial hyperplasia with atypia in females
administered ≥60 mg/kg/day, which correlated with increased uterus/cervix weights. In
addition, an increase in the incidence of malignant lymphoma was noted in females
administered 60 or 80 mg/kg/day (statistically significant only for females administered 80
mg/kg/day). Decreased incidences (not statistically significant) of mammary neoplasms
(fibroadenoma, adenoma, and/or adenocarcinoma), with a concurrent decrease in the
occurrence of physiological hyperplasia and atypical hyperplasia in the mammary
gland, and a decreased occurrence of pituitary and thyroid C-cell adenomas were noted in
females administered ≥60 mg/kg/day.

Data Quality

tumor.xpt datafile.
3.2.2

Survival Analysis

The survival distributions of rates in all treatment groups were estimated using the KaplanMeier product limit method. For control, low, medium, and high dose groups, the dose
response relationship was tested using the likelihood ratio test and the homogeneity of survival
distributions were tested using the log-rank test. The Kaplan-Meier curves for survival rates are
given in Figures 1A in the appendix. The intercurrent mortality data are given in Tables 1A in
the appendix. Results of the tests for dose response relationship and homogeneity of survivals,
are given in Tables 3A in the appendix.
Reviewer’s findings: The female rats were terminated at Week 104. This reviewer’s analysis
showed the numbers (percent) of death that occurred prior to termination of the group were 56
(56%), 61 (61%), 62 (62%), 58 (58%), or 63 (63%) rats in the VC, LD, ML, MH, or HD groups,
respectively. The survival analyses didn’t show any statistically significant dose response
relationship in the mortality of females.

3.2.3

Page 8 of 22

Tumor Data Analysis

The tumor data were analyzed for dose response relationships and pairwise comparisons of
control group with each of the treated groups. Both the dose response relationship tests and
pairwise comparisons were performed using the Poly-k method described in the papers of
Bailer and Portier [2] and Bieler and Williams [3]. In this method an animal that lives the full
study period ( wmax ) or dies before the terminal sacrifice but develops the tumor type being
tested gets a score of sh =1. An animal that dies at week wh without developing the tumor
k

before the end of the study gets a score of sh =  wh  <1. The adjusted group size is defined as
w 
 max 

Σ sh . As an interpretation, an animal with score sh =1 can be considered as a whole animal
while an animal with score sh < 1 can be considered as a partial animal. The adjusted group size
Σ sh is equal to N (the original group size) if all animals live up to the end of the study or if each
animal that dies before the terminal sacrifice develops at least one tumor of the tumor type
being tested, otherwise the adjusted group size is less than N. These adjusted group sizes are
then used for the dose response relationship (or the pairwise) tests using the Cochran-Armitage
test. One critical point for Poly-k test is the choice of the appropriate value of k, which depends
on the tumor incidence pattern with the increased dose. For long term 104-week standard rat
and mouse studies, a value of k=3 is suggested in the literature. Hence, this reviewer used k=3
for the analysis of this data. For the calculation of p-values the exact permutation method was
used.
The adjusted levels of significance for testing a positive dose response in the 2-year rat study
are 0.005 and 0.025 for a common tumor and a rare tumor, respectively. The adjusted levels
of significance for the pairwise comparisons in the 2-year rat study are 0.01 and 0.05 for a
common tumor and a rare tumor, respectively. A rare tumor is defined as one in which the
tumor rate is less than 1% in the vehicle control group. The tumor incidences rates and the
p-values of the tested tumor types are listed in Tables 5A in the appendix.
Reviewer’s findings: Following table displays the tumor types showing p-values less than
or equal to 0.05 either for dose response relationships or for pairwise comparisons of treated
groups and control.

Executive CAC Final Study Minutes
Date of Meeting: December 10, 2024
Committee: Karen Davis Bruno, PhD, OND IO, Chair
Paul Brown, PhD, OND IO, Member
Tim McGovern, PhD, OND IO, Member
Ron Wange, PhD, OND IO, Member

The following information reflects a brief summary of the Committee discussion and its
recommendations.
Application Type and Number(s): NDA 219469
Drug Name: Elinzanetant
Applicant: Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.
Background
Elinzanetant (BAY 3427080; NT-814; 7486; GSK 1144814A) is a Neurokinin (NK) 1 and
NK3 receptor antagonist being proposed for the treatment of moderate to severe
vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause. The Applicant submitted the final
study reports for the 104-week rat carcinogenicity study and the 26-week transgenic
rasH2 (Tg.rasH2) mouse study. The dose selections for both the rat and transgenic
mouse studies were as per the Executive CAC recommendation (Refer to ExecCAC
Meeting Minutes, Oct 19, 2020, for rat study and ExecCAC Meeting Minutes, Dec 06,
2022, for mouse study). The Applicant had previously submitted complete reports of a
full battery of genotoxicity studies including an Ames test, an in-vitro mouse lymphoma
L5178Y cell assay, and an in-vivo rat micronucleus assay, which did not reveal any
evidence of a genotoxic potential of elinzanetant. The three principal elinzanetant
metabolites M27, M30/34, and M18/21 also generated no genotoxicity signals in in-vitro
and in-vivo assays.
Mouse Carcinogenicity Study
The Tg.rasH2 mouse carcinogenicity study was conducted in both male and female
mice for the duration of 26 weeks. Elinzanetant was administered at doses 0 (vehicle:
1% aqueous methylcellulose), 10, 30, 85 mg/kg/day in males and 0, 10, 20, 70
mg/kg/day in females via oral gavage. The data was analyzed by the FDA statistical
reviewer, Feng Zhou, MS, Division of Biometrics VI. There were no statistically
significant relationships by trend or pair-wise analysis for the incidence of any tumor in
male or female mice. Elinzanetant did not affect the overall survival rate, nor did it
produce adverse clinical signs up to the high dose of 85 mg/kg/day in males and 70
1

5500305
Reference ID: 5523839

mg/kg/day in females. The positive control, a single dose of N-methyl-N-nitrosourea
(MNU) at 75 mg/kg by IP injection on Day 1, resulted in the expected tumor response.
Rat Carcinogenicity Study
The rat carcinogenicity study was conducted in female Sprague-Dawley rats for the
duration of 104 weeks. The Applicant conducted the study at the ExecCAC
recommended doses: 0 (vehicle: 1% aqueous methylcellulose), 7, 20, and 60
mg/kg/day doses and added an additional 80 mg/kg/day group. Because elinzanetant is
being developed for the clinical indication of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms
in postmenopausal women, the study was conducted only in female rats per the
ExecCAC suggestion. The FDA statistical reviewer Feng Zhou, MS, Division of
Biometrics VI, reviewed the tumor data. At ≥60 mg/kg/day, elinzanetant caused
statistically significant increases, by both trend and pairwise analysis, in the incidence
of: i) malignant lymphoma in the hematolymphoid system (80 mg/kg/day only); ii)
malignant endometrial adenocarcinoma of the uterus; iii) combined malignant and
benign endometrial tumors in the uterus; and iv) combined malignant and benign
endometrial tumors and malignant squamous cell carcinoma in the uterus. The lowest
dose of elinzanetant associated with significantly increased incidence of tumors was 60
mg/kg/day. Based on AUCs, the clinical exposure margins provided by this dose to the
Maximum Recommended Human Dose (MRHD) of 120 mg/day is ~29.4x for
elinzanetant and ~7.0x for M30/34 (the predominant metabolite in humans and
animals). There was no statistically significant dose-response relationship for mortality,
though a dose-dependent reduction of body weight gain was observed with elinzanetant
treatment.

Application Type and Number(s): IND 129492
Drug Name: Elinzanetant (BAY 3427080, NT-814, GSK1144814A) capsule
Sponsor: Bayer Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals
Background
BAY 3247080 (elinzanetant, NT-814) is an antagonist of both the human neurokinin
(NK)1 and NK3 receptors that is in development for the treatment of moderate to severe
vasomotor symptoms in postmenopausal women. In nonclinical studies, the drug
product is administered by oral gavage on a BID (twice daily) dosing schedule.
BAY 3427080 was negative for genetic toxicity in a full battery of in vitro (Ames and
mouse lymphoma L5178Y TK+/- assay) and in vivo (rat bone marrow micronucleus
assay) studies.
BAY 3427080 is cleared primarily by the liver. Analysis of patient plasma from phase 2
clinical studies identified three metabolites accounting for more than 10% of total drug
AUC. These metabolites are M27, M18/21, and M30/34. They exhibit high affinity and
activity at the human NK1 and NK3 receptors that is similar to the affinity and activity of
elinzanetant in in vitro binding and cellular functional assays. The sponsor has
conducted appropriate chronic repeat-dose toxicity studies with BAY 3427080 (parent)
in rats and monkeys and with the M27 metabolite specifically in rats that provide
adequate safety qualification for all of the disproportionate metabolites at a clinical
maximum daily dose of 120 mg/day.

2

Reference ID: 5523839
5090934

In vitro genetic toxicology studies were also conducted for the disproportionate human
metabolites. M27, M30/34, and M18/21 were negative for mutagenic effect in in vitro
bacterial reverse mutation assays and in vitro micronucleus assays.
Mouse Carcinogenicity Study Dose Selection
Bayer proposed a 26-week study in the Tg-rasH2 mouse at doses of 10, 30, and 100
mg/kg to be administered BID yielding total daily doses of 20, 60, and 200 mg/kg/d.
The control group will be dosed with the vehicle, 1% aqueous methylcellulose. A single
75 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose of N-methyl-N-nitrosourea will be administered to positive
control groups.
Dose selection was based on maximum tolerated dose (MTD), determined in two 28day GLP studies, the first conducted in wild type Tg-rasH2 mice (T1-5264-8) and the
second in the transgenic strain (T105617-0 unaudited draft).
In the first study, doses of 10, 30, or 100 mg/kg/dose BID (i.e., 20, 60, and 200 mg/kg/d)
were well-tolerated for the majority of animals. However, 3 out of 12 high-dose females
were prematurely sacrificed due to poor condition and severe body weight losses of -16
to -21% on Days 8 to 15, indicating that 200 mg/kg/d exceeded the MTD in females.
Two to three unscheduled sacrifices also occurred at each of the low and mid-doses
and in the control group. The MTD for males was 200 mg/kg/d in this study. The
sponsor’s NOAEL for males and females was set at the low dose: 20 mg/kg/d. At the
high dose of 200 mg/kg/d, on day 28, an exposure multiple of 10.8x (based on AUC0-24)
was achieved relative to the proposed clinical human dose of 120 mg/day.
In the second study in transgenic Tg-rasH2 mice, the sponsor explored doses around
the MTDs observed in the wild-type Tg-rasH2 mice to better define an appropriate highdose selection: 0, 150, 200, 250 mg/kg/d. The high dose of 250 mg/kg/d led to
moribund condition and death in all males, which was attributed to BAY 3427080related systemic atrophy of adipose tissue and skeletal muscle degeneration. Doses of
up to 200 mg/kg/d in males and 250 mg/kg/d in females were otherwise generally well
tolerated in the transgenic strain. Sponsor’s NOAEL for males was set at 200 mg/kg/d,
and for females, 250 mg/kg/d.

Background
NT-814 is an antagonist of both the human neurokinin (NK)1 and NK3 receptors
developed by Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals for the treatment of moderate to severe
vasomotor symptoms in post-menopausal women. A submission to IND 129492 dated
September 4, 2020, contained a draft protocol for a 104-week carcinogenicity study that
the Sponsor proposes to conduct administering NT-814 twice daily by oral gavage in
Sprague Dawley rats. NT-814 was neither genotoxic nor clastogenic in an adequate
battery of in vitro and in vivo assays.
Rat Carcinogenicity Study Dose Selection
The data submitted to support dose selection for the carcinogenicity study comprise two
oral chronic toxicity studies in Sprague Dawley rats of 13- and 26- weeks duration. The
doses proposed by the Sponsor are different between sexes because the rate of NT-814
metabolism is greater in males than in females.

Executive CAC Recommendations and Conclusions
 The Committee recommended doses of 0 [aqueous solution of 1% methylcellulose
(viscosity 400 cP)], 7, 20, and 60 mg/kg/twice daily (via oral gavage) for female
rats only with the high dose based on achieving an AUC ratio greater than 25-fold
of the clinical exposure. The mid- and low- doses were selected based on
adequate spacing of AUC.
 The Committee noted that if the clinical dose changes such that the exposure
ratio is no longer at least 25-fold at the high dose, then the study may not be
acceptable.
 For male rats, the Committee could not concur on doses because an MTD was not
established in the 26-week study or in the 13-week study, which had many
discrepancies. The Sponsor would need to conduct and submit a new dose range
finding study for ECAC concurrence on dose selection for male rats. Alternately,
the Sponsor could increase the number of female rats proposed in the 2-year study
and not include a male group because the indication is for moderate to severe
vasomotor symptoms in postmenopausal females.
 The Committee noted that the Sponsor submitted a draft report for the 26-week
toxicity study. The current recommendations provided by the Committee are
contingent on the results of the final report not being notably different from those
in the draft report, such that dose recommendations might have differed.
 If there are survival issues during the study, the Sponsor should contact the
Review Division before any changes are made.
